text: A friend of yours and mine has very justly defined good-breeding to be, THE RESULT OF MUCH GOOD SENSE, SOME GOOD NATURE, AND A LITTLE SELF-DENIAL FOR THE SAKE OF OTHERS, AND WITH A VIEW TO OBTAIN THE SAME INDULGENCE FROM THEM.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXXVIII, to his son, London, November 3, Old Style 1749
